subject: Post-call: HealthScope model fit + safety evals / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Priya Rao <priya@healthscope.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@healthscope.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: HealthScope model fit + safety evals / next steps

Hi Priya / Tom —

Thanks again for the conversation today — appreciated the context on HealthScope's clinical triage and internal compliance needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Recap (30 min call):
- Primary goal: integrate an LLM assistant into intake triage to summarize patient-reported symptoms and recommend next best action (triage category only; no definitive medical advice).
- Key constraints: strict refusal for clinical advice beyond triage, audit logs for decisions, and data residency in US region.
- Success metrics: >= 85% triage-category match vs. clinician labels on a 2k-sample eval; latency P95 <= 350ms at target QPS.

Recommended model variants for initial evals:
- redwood-rlm-8k-qlora (cost/latency-optimized; good for structured triage outputs)
- open-llama-13b-guard (higher-quality, stronger refusal patterns in our safety finetune)
- redwood-rlm-16k-safety (for sessions where longer context + safety prompts required)

Attached / linked artifacts:
- redwood-eval-benchmarks.csv (initial benchmark run on a synthetic triage set)
- model-prompt-set.md (suggested prompt templates and guardrail prompts we tested)
- rdw-security-SOC2.pdf (SOC 2 overview + how we handle audit logs)

Ask / next steps:
1) If you can share a redacted sample of 200 triage examples (CSV with columns: patient_id, narrative, clinician_label) we can run a quick fit/eval and return: per-model confusion matrix, refusal rate on sensitive prompts, and prompt tuning recommendations (ETA: 5 business days).
2) Dev/infra sync: can we schedule a 30-min POC kickoff next week to validate latency and data residency? Suggested times Wed/Thu next week; we can send a calendar invite once you confirm.
3) Procurement: I included our SOC2 + standard MSA in the linked drive; happy to walk procurement through the controls.

Dev (cc'd) — can you call out any immediate limitations re: data residency and logging retention we should flag for Priya?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

(attachments: redwood-eval-benchmarks.csv, model-prompt-set.md, rdw-security-SOC2.pdf)

From: Dr. Priya Rao <priya@healthscope.com>

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: HealthScope model fit + safety evals / next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few follow-ups from our side:

1) Safety / refusal behavior: we need to ensure the model consistently refuses when asked for medical advice beyond triage (e.g., diagnosis, prescriptions). Can you provide evidence from the evals that show refusal rates and types of failure modes? Specifically: false-positive refusals vs. false-negative refusals, and examples of prompt-engineered guardrails that you recommend.

2) Data residency & audit logs: our legal team requires confirmation that training data will not be retained, and that all inference logs (input + output) can be stored in our VPC for a minimum of 12 months for audit. Is that supported in your Private/Dedicated options, or would we need a separate SOW?

3) Procurement asked for SOC2 report and typical contract/terms for a Dedicated deployment. I've attached our procurement questionnaire (redacted).

We can share the 200 redacted examples but want to lock in the safety guardrails before moving data. Also — can you share any examples of medical-domain refusal tests you ran in-house?

Thanks,
Priya

Dr. Priya Rao
Head of Clinical Products | HealthScope
priya@healthscope.com
(attachment: HealthScope_SGQ_redacted.pdf)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Priya Rao <priya@healthscope.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: HealthScope model fit + safety evals / next steps

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the questions. Quick technical answers and references to the artifacts Marissa shared.

1) Refusal behavior / safety controls:
- We run targeted refusal suites that include ~1k adversarial prompts (medical diagnosis, harmful recommendations, step-by-step procedural instructions). For each model variant we measure: refusal rate, hallucination rate (factuality on gold set), and prompt-conditional outputs. The redwood-eval-benchmarks.csv includes a per-prompt breakdown and tagged failure-mode (see column "failure_mode").
- Guardrails we recommend: prompt-layer refusal templates (examples in model-prompt-set.md), a lightweight post-generation classifier (safety-refusal-layer) that flags outputs for forced refusal, and a hard fallback to a canned refusal statement when confidence < threshold.

2) Data residency & logs:
- Dedicated / Private deployment supports customer-controlled VPC where inference request/response logs can be retained in the customer's project with configurable retention (we can set 12 months). We do not ingest your data into our model training pipelines unless explicitly agreed in writing (we can put this in the SOW).

3) SOC2 & procurement docs:
- The rdw-security-SOC2.pdf in the drive is our attestations summary. For Dedicated deployments we provide an SOC2 packaged report under NDA; we can share the full report with your security team.

4) Practical testing suggestion:
- If you share the 200-row sample we will run the three recommended model variants and send: per-example outputs, refusal labels, confusion matrix, and a short prompt-tuning recommendation doc. We'll also include examples of prompts where the model incorrectly offers medical advice so you can see failure modes.

Copying David (infra/security) to confirm the VPC/logging details if you want exact retention SLAs.

—Dev

Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
